q: Quantum money (Wiesner, 1969/1983) proposes bank notes with quantum states that cannot be counterfeited due to the no-cloning theorem. The challenge for public-key quantum money is:
opts: The bank must verify the note, which requires a way to check the quantum state without revealing it — this is the 'collision resistance' requirement for a quantum one-way function
Quantum money is equivalent to classical money
exp: Public quantum money requires a verification algorithm that can test validity without revealing the state (so that counterfeiters cannot learn it from multiple verification queries). Constructing secure public quantum money under standard cryptographic assumptions is an open problem.
